summary: Completed frontend-only regression and code review for ASCII rollout, motion behavior, route/navigation integrity, demo execution, waitlist UI flow, mobile readability, and reduced-motion accessibility on the public preview URL.

integration_issues.flow: ASCII asset fetch during rapid hard navigations/reloads
integration_issues.issue: Observed REQUEST FAILED net::ERR_ABORTED entries in browser automation console logs when page transitions interrupt in-flight ASCII text fetches.

issues: Hover effects are still broadly defined outside pointer-scoped media blocks; only part of hover motion is gated by @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine).

action_items: Scope all non-essential hover-only animation styles under fine-pointer media queries to fully match touch-safe motion requirement.
Consider handling/canceling in-flight AsciiBackdrop fetch requests explicitly (e.g., AbortController) and suppressing benign abort noise for cleaner console behavior during route transitions.
critical_code_review_comments: AsciiBackdrop swallows fetch failures and silently falls back; this hides asset delivery issues from observability. Consider lightweight diagnostics/telemetry for failed asset loads.
The touch-safe hover requirement is only partially implemented: several :hover rules remain globally active outside pointer gating.
test_credentials: Read /app/memory/test_credentials.md (auth not implemented/required for this app).
seed_data_creation: Filled waitlist form fields in UI checks (no confirmed submission persisted in this run).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Exact ASCII art was confirmed for hero/legal/resources/article/use-case/final CTA, but some routes require a short wait for async text fetch completion before asserting length. Demo run reached complete state, 10 use-case routes loaded, legal/resources/article navigation passed, mobile overflow checks passed, and prefers-reduced-motion computed animation state was disabled (0s/none).
rca of the issue: RCA-1: net::ERR_ABORTED entries are reproducible when hard navigation/reload interrupts in-flight public ASCII text fetch requests. This is timing-related (not persistent asset outage): direct URL probes and delayed in-page checks returned HTTP 200 and full text lengths. Mitigation: cancel in-flight fetches intentionally and treat AbortError as expected during unmount/navigation, plus avoid immediate strict assertions before async content settles.
